papers.title_in_file: Testing and learning structured quantum Hamiltonians
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 1.4 discussion and open questions; proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper giving query-efficient algorithms for testing and learning local and sparse Hamiltonians, with and without quantum memory.

assertions.value: The authors state that their learning algorithms can be run without quantum memory, at the cost of squaring the query complexity, with an extra (log n) factor for local Hamiltonians and an n factor for sparse Hamiltonians.
quotes: We give subroutines that allow us to reproduce all the above learning results without quantum memory; squaring the query complexity and paying a (log n)-factor in the local case and an n-factor in the sparse case.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a proved result in the abstract; subroutines in Section 3.3 and Section 5.1

assertions.value: The authors state that their learning results have no dependence on the system size n but require n-qubit quantum memory.
quotes: The learning results stated above have no dependence on the system size n, but require n-qubit quantum memory.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its own memory-based learning results in the abstract

assertions.value: The authors state that the protocols are not shown to be robust to SPAM noise, and list this as a desirable future step.
quotes: It would be desirable to make the protocols introduced in this work to be robust to SPAM noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1.4 open question 2, p.8

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Kernels are Spectral Tensor Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, main text, numerical section and discussion; appendix proofs skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A letter showing that the Fourier representation of a quantum kernel is a matrix product operator, and testing its compressibility numerically.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the finite Fourier expansion of any quantum kernel can be written as an ETK contraction whose entries are the Fourier coefficients, so an exact MPO factorization of the coefficients gives a spectral tensor network representation of the kernel.
quotes: First, the finite Fourier expansion of any quantum kernel can be written directly as an ETK contraction, with the ETK entries given precisely by the Fourier coefficients.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as an exact identity in the introduction, proved in the appendix

assertions.value: The authors report that for L = 6 layers the kernel target alignment rises quickly with bond dimension and approaches unity for both d = 2 and d = 3, on the frequency-resolving grid and on independently sampled test points.
quotes: Fig. 3(a) shows that, for L = 6 layers, the alignment increases rapidly with bond dimension and approaches unity for both d = 2 and d = 3, on both the frequencyresolving grid and independently sampled test points.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on random layered feature maps, Fig. 3
assertions.reader_inference: The authors read the result as a diagnostic of whether kernel evaluation is classically tractable for these kernels.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical evidence for small bond dimension is restricted to the random layered feature maps they considered.
quotes: The numerical evidence for small bond dimension, however, is restricted to the random layered feature maps considered here.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own scope statement in the numerical section

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Optimizing Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Sensor Circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results table and conclusion; middle method sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study using reinforcement learning with Qiskit and Tket to optimize entanglement layout and circuit size in small quantum sensor circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report QFI and entropy in the range of 0.84-1.0 together with depth and gate count reductions of 20- 86% in their simulated circuits.
quotes: measuring high QFI and entropy in the range of 0.84-1.0 with depth and gates count reduction by 20- 86%
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study simulation result stated in the abstract and Table 4
assertions.reader_inference: The conclusion gives the QFI and entropy range as 0.8 to 1.0, which differs from the abstract range.

assertions.value: The authors state that the optimization algorithm has exponential complexity in the number of qubits, and that simulations up to 20 qubits were successful while larger systems remain challenging.
quotes: The optimization algorithm exhibits exponential complexity with respect to the number of qubits.
While simulations up to 20 qubits were successful, scaling to larger systems remain challenging.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own stated limit in the conclusion

assertions.value: The authors list testing and validating the optimized circuits on real quantum hardware as future work.
quotes: Extending our work to test and validate the optimized quantum circuits on real quantum hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own future-work statement in the conclusion

papers.version_note: File is arXiv v2, 3 May 2025; the record id carries 2026
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results (numerical experiments, quantum advantage section), conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A proposal of a Markov-network-informed quantum circuit Born machine ansatz, tested numerically against problem-agnostic circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that on random graphs with communities their QCMRF models reach better performance than problem-agnostic QCIBMs while using fewer trainable parameters.
quotes: Here our QCMRF models reach better performance than the problem-agnostic QCIBMs, while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters, since they exploit the sparsity of the graph.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation results, Fig. 4

assertions.value: The authors report that for the 10-node graphs the QCIBM model has 85 parameters, while the QCMRF circuits have 60, 58 and 66.
quotes: For these 10-node graphs, the corresponding QCIBM model has 85 parameters, while the QCMRF circuits only have 60, 58 and 66 respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Reported counts for the circuits the authors built

assertions.value: The authors state an informal conjecture that the QCMRF circuit class contains classically hard cases and so yields a quantum advantage in sampling; they do not prove it.
assertions.anchor: Section on potential for quantum advantage
quotes: Informal Conjecture. The class of QCMRF circuits, that can learn probability distributions efficiently represented by MNs, also contains classically hard cases, yielding a quantum advantage in sampling.
assertions.certainty_reason: Labeled an informal conjecture by the authors

papers.title_in_file: No Reference-Free Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, theorem statements, discussion; appendix proofs and numerics skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving that a quantum learner without an external reference frame cannot generalize to pure states outside the span of its training states.

assertions.value: The paper proves that when the training states do not span the full Hilbert space, all pure states orthogonal to their span must receive the same prediction.
quotes: We prove that whenever the training states fail to span the full Hilbert space, all pure states orthogonal to their span must receive the same prediction
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2 (no off-span quantum generalization)

assertions.value: The authors state that learning generic unstructured concepts on multiqubit systems requires exponentially many independently oriented training directions.
quotes: show that learning generic unstructured concepts on multiqubit systems requires exponentially many independently oriented training directions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 4 (reference-rank lower bound)

assertions.value: The authors state that the reference-free model is intentionally not a description of every QML algorithm.
quotes: The resulting model is intentionally not a description of every QML algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own scope statement in the introduction
assertions.reader_inference: Practical models that supply a basis, feature map or observable fall outside the no-go result.

papers.title_in_file: Probabilistic modeling over permutations using quantum computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion; appendices and algorithm details skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A quantum algorithm design that encodes a probabilistic model over permutations into a quantum state using the QFT over the symmetric group.

assertions.value: The authors construct a quantum algorithm that encodes the exact probabilistic model over permutations, which they describe as a classically intractable object, into the amplitudes of a quantum state using the QFT over the symmetric group.
quotes: into the amplitudes of a quantum state by making use of the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) over the symmetric group.
assertions.certainty_reason: Algorithm design under stated assumptions; no run

assertions.value: The authors state that they have not provided empirical evidence comparing the model against classical bandlimited implementations or other non-spectral heuristics on real-world datasets.
quotes: Additionally, we have not yet provided empirical evidence comparing the model's performance against classical bandlimited implementations or other non-spectral heuristics on real-world datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own limitation in the discussion

assertions.value: The authors state that rigorous analytical bounds on the QSVT success probability are generally impossible without strong assumptions about the data-generating process and are beyond the scope of the work.
quotes: Providing rigorous analytical bounds on this success probability is generally impossible without strong assumptions regarding the underlying data-generating process, and thus remains beyond the scope of this work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own scope statement

papers.title_in_file: On the mathematical structure of quantum models of computation based on Hamiltonian minimisation (doctoral dissertation)
papers.version_note: File is the doctoral dissertation (Skoltech, 2021), long; only the front matter, introduction, main statements and conclusion were read
papers.partial_detail: Contents, introduction, main statements defended, conclusion, start of Chapter 1; chapter proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A dissertation on Hamiltonian ground-state computation, covering Ising and QMA-hard constructions, ZX tensor rewriting and the universality of variational quantum computation.

assertions.value: The author states as a main defended result the establishment of the computational universality of the variational model of quantum computation.
quotes: The development of the mathematical model to describe variational quantum computation and the establishment of the computational universality of the variational model of quantum computation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a defended claim; proof in Chapter 5 not read

assertions.value: The author states as a main defended result a proof that physically relevant Hamiltonians can embed universal quantum computational resources for ground state quantum computation.
quotes: can embed universal quantum computational resources for ground state quantum computation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a defended claim; proof not read

assertions.value: The author states that the anticipated computational resources for determining ground state energy and for calculating energy relative to a state are conjectured, not proved.
quotes: Anticipated computational resources to determine ground state energy and calculate energy relative to a state have been conjectured.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's own conjecture label in the conclusion

papers.title_in_file: Utilizing small quantum computers for machine learning and ground state energy approximation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, conclusion; appendix derivations not read
papers.what_it_is: A quantum circuit partitioning method that measures an observable on a large system using several smaller quantum systems, tested on an Ising ground state and digit classification.

assertions.value: The authors report a relative error of the order of 0.1% in the ground state energy of the transverse-field Ising model for all tested system sizes of n = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 spins.
quotes: we achieved a relative error within the order of 0.1% for all the tested system sizes of n = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 spins.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result, Fig. 4

assertions.value: The authors report that classifying the digits 3 and 6 generalized to out-of-sample data with 100% accuracy.
quotes: When applied to the classification between the digits 3 and 6, we were able to generalize to out-of-sample data with 100% accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single two-class experiment

assertions.value: The authors state that performance in the presence of noise like that of current quantum devices remains to be investigated.
quotes: Additionally, we would like to investigate the performance of our method in the presence of noise akin to currently available quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own future-work statement in the conclusion
